title: Felix and the Cipher
premise: When the coffin of Ashford's revered founder, Edmund Vane, is found empty during a cemetery relocation, retired detective Jonah Yarrow is pulled back into a case the town buried forty years ago. Following a cipher hidden in first-edition books from his own failing shop, Jonah uncovers that Vane faked his death to escape accomplices in a land-fraud scheme—and that several of Ashford's most respected families have been paying for his silence ever since. As witnesses die and the town closes ranks, Jonah realizes the empty coffin was opened deliberately, as a message: someone wants the past exhumed. In the end, Jonah confronts the last living conspirator—his own former mentor, now the town's dying patriarch—and must choose between exposing a truth that will destroy Ashford or letting the dead keep their secrets.
about_author: Rosalind Voss is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing small-town records before turning to fiction full-time. She writes mysteries about the weight of history, drawing on her fascination with the documents people leave behind and the ones they burn.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet
chapters.summary: Jonah Yarrow opens his struggling bookshop on a gray morning, establishing his deliberate invisibility after retiring from the force under a cloud of scandal. A routine order of estate-sale books arrives, including a strange annotated first edition. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: weary contentment about to crack.

chapters.title: Ground Broken
chapters.summary: The town gathers for the ceremonial relocation of founder Edmund Vane's remains to make way for a new civic center. Jonah attends out of obligation, observing old rivals and the imperious Vane family matriarch, Cordelia. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: unease beneath civic pride.

chapters.title: Empty
chapters.summary: Gravediggers find the coffin sealed but vacant—no body, no explanation, only a rotted leather satchel. Police chief Dana Okafor, who once worked under Jonah, reluctantly asks him to consult. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: the pull of an unsolvable puzzle.

chapters.title: Forty Years of Dust
chapters.summary: Jonah reviews the original 1984 death file at the station and notices discrepancies: no autopsy photographs, a rushed coroner's sign-off by Dr. Harlan Pike, now elderly and reclusive. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: professional instinct reawakening against his will.

chapters.title: The Annotated Edition
chapters.summary: At home, Jonah studies the first edition from the estate sale and finds marginalia in a substitution cipher, signed with a single letter: E.V. The annotations reference locations around town. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: cold thrill of connection.

chapters.title: Cordelia's Grief
chapters.summary: Jonah interviews Cordelia Vane, who insists her father is buried where he belongs and warns him off with chilling composure. Her son Marcus watches the interview too intently. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: sensing performance rather than grief.

chapters.title: Pike's Confession Half-Made
chapters.summary: Dr. Pike, in a care home, tells Jonah he signed what he was told to sign, then clams up, terrified. He mentions 'the ledger' before his nurse ends the visit. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: pity curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: First Marker
chapters.summary: Deciphering the book's clues leads Jonah to the old mill ruins, where he finds a weatherproof tin containing a second coded page and a photograph of five men, faces scratched out except one: young Harlan Pike. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: dread compounding.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Watcher
chapters.summary: Someone has been in the shop overnight; nothing stolen, but the cipher book has been moved. Jonah installs a camera and finds a figure he almost recognizes. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: violation—the invisibility he chose is gone.

chapters.title: Okafor's Pressure
chapters.summary: Chief Okafor reveals the mayor wants the empty-coffin matter closed as vandalism. She privately admits she never believed the original file either. POV: alternating Jonah/Okafor. Emotional beat: fragile alliance formed.

chapters.title: Five Men
chapters.summary: Jonah identifies the photo's era through newspaper archives: Vane and four partners in the Ashford Development Company, which bought floodplain land cheaply before a dam project made it valuable. One partner died young; another moved away. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: the shape of a conspiracy emerging.

chapters.title: Marcus Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Marcus visits the shop offering a consulting fee to 'advise' the family and subtly probes what Jonah knows. Jonah declines and lies smoothly—a skill he thought rusted. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: temptation and self-disgust.

chapters.title: The Drowned Field
chapters.summary: A cipher clue leads to the reservoir; diving volunteers later recover a locked strongbox containing the Development Company's real ledger, showing payoffs flowing to town officials for decades. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by scale of corruption.

chapters.title: Death of a Witness
chapters.summary: Dr. Pike is found dead—an apparent fall down stairs—hours after Jonah's visit becomes known. Guilt hits Jonah hard; he realizes his questions painted a target. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: grief and responsibility.

chapters.title: Closed Ranks
chapters.summary: Town council moves to condemn the cemetery dig as complete and seal records. Old friends stop meeting Jonah's eyes. His shop's lease is suddenly 'under review.' POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: isolation deepening.

chapters.title: Rosalind's Letters
chapters.summary: Sorting the estate-sale collection, Jonah discovers the seller was Rosalind Marsh, Vane's long-dead secretary, whose letters hint she kept copies of everything—and feared for her life. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: a ghost ally emerging.

chapters.title: The Second Cipher
chapters.summary: Marsh's letters contain their own code, keyed to hymn numbers from the Methodist church. Decoded, they reveal Vane didn't die in 1984—he fled, and Marsh helped him. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: the case inverting entirely.

chapters.title: Alive, Then
chapters.summary: If Vane lived, someone has been receiving his silence payments—or impersonating him. Jonah traces pension-like transfers routed through a shell charity still active today. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: vertigo of a rewritten history.

chapters.title: Night Visitor
chapters.summary: The watcher returns; Jonah's camera catches him clearly: Walter Finch, the town historian, terrified and apologetic. Finch confesses he's been paid for years to maintain the official archive—editing it. POV: Jonah/Finch. Emotional beat: reluctant confession.

chapters.title: What Finch Kept
chapters.summary: Finch surrenders originals he secretly preserved: minutes proving the five partners voted to fake Vane's death when federal investigators closed in, splitting the assets while Vane vanished abroad. POV: Finch flashback via Jonah's reading. Emotional beat: the machinery of the lie laid bare.

chapters.title: The Fourth Man
chapters.summary: Of the five partners, three are dead. The fourth, Gerald Hoyt, left town in 1990—but Jonah finds evidence Hoyt returned under a new name and now sits on the council pushing the civic center project. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: the enemy wearing a neighbor's face.

chapters.title: Councilman Aldous Reed
chapters.summary: Jonah confronts Councilman Aldous Reed (Hoyt's assumed name) obliquely at a public hearing. Reed smiles, denies everything, and that night the shop's window is smashed. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: open war declared.

chapters.title: Okafor Sidelined
chapters.summary: Okafor is suspended pending an 'integrity review' orchestrated by the mayor. Before leaving, she gives Jonah the one thing she kept: the original coroner's signature page, with a second signature underneath, partially erased. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: the institution itself corrupted.

chapters.title: Under the Signature
chapters.summary: Forensic work on the erased signature suggests it belongs to someone still prominent. Cross-referencing hymn-cipher letters, Jonah lands on a name he refuses to believe: Chief Ellery Nash, his own mentor, retired and beloved. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: personal devastation.

chapters.title: Mentor
chapters.summary: Jonah visits Nash at his lakeside home. The old man is sharp, warm, and lying. He admits he knew about the scheme, took payments to bury the file, and claims he did it to protect the town from ruin. POV: Jonah/Nash. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Nash's Bargain
chapters.summary: Nash offers Jonah the full story in exchange for silence: Vane came back in 2001, dying, and demanded the payments continue to his caretaker. Nash has been the conduit ever since. He warns Jonah that Cordelia will kill to end it. POV: Jonah/Nash. Emotional beat: poisoned truth-telling.

chapters.title: Who Opened the Coffin
chapters.summary: Reassembling motives, Jonah deduces the exhumation wasn't accidental exposure—it was staged. Someone wanted the coffin found empty to force the secret open and destroy the others. Only one person benefits: Marcus Vane, who learned he'd been cut from the payments. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: the mystery's true question surfacing.

chapters.title: Finch Disappears
chapters.summary: Walter Finch vanishes; his house shows signs of hurried departure, not abduction—except his archive copies are gone. Jonah realizes Finch sold out or was turned. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: allies are currency here, spent freely.

chapters.title: The Caretaker
chapters.summary: Tracing the shell charity's final beneficiary, Jonah finds a private nursing cottage outside town housing a silent, stroke-ridden old man who may or may not be Edmund Vane himself, kept alive as leverage. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: horror at what power preserves.

chapters.title: Cordelia Unmasked
chapters.summary: Jonah confronts Cordelia with the ledger. She breaks—not with guilt but fury: her father abandoned them, faked death, and let her spend a lifetime defending a lie. She admits she's known since 2001 and has been paying to keep him hidden and quiet. POV: Cordelia/Jonah. Emotional beat: rage as grief.

chapters.title: Threats Converge
chapters.summary: Marcus, learning Jonah met his mother, sends thugs to burn the bookshop. Jonah saves the rare-book room but loses nearly everything else, including the cipher book—though he photographed every page. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: loss crystallizing resolve.

chapters.title: Restoring Okafor
chapters.summary: Jonah delivers the erased-signature evidence to the state attorney general's office, bypassing local power entirely. An outside investigator arrives; Okafor is reinstated. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: institutions can be fought, slowly.

chapters.title: The Hymn at Midnight
chapters.summary: A final decoded message from Marsh, dated the week she drowned in 1988, names where she hid her master copy: inside the church organ, in the hymn-number chamber. Jonah retrieves it with the pastor's reluctant help. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: the dead testifying at last.

chapters.title: Everything, Documented
chapters.summary: Marsh's cache proves the fraud, the payoffs, Nash's cover-up, and—crucially—that Vane's 'death' certificate was signed by Nash personally. It also names Gerald Hoyt as the partner who tried to blackmail the others and disappeared. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: completeness, and its terrible weight.

chapters.title: Reed Runs
chapters.summary: Exposed, Aldous Reed attempts to flee with the charity's remaining funds; Okafor arrests him at the bus depot. Under interrogation he confirms everything and points at Marcus as the one who staged the exhumation. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: the net closing.

chapters.title: Marcus's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Cornered, Marcus takes Cordelia hostage at the Vane house, demanding the ledger be destroyed so the family name survives intact. Jonah talks him down using the truth Marcus actually craves: that his grandfather's legacy was always a lie worth less than his own life. POV: Jonah/Marcus. Emotional beat: climax—identity versus inheritance.

chapters.title: The Man in the Cottage
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, DNA confirms the nursing-home patient is Edmund Vane. He dies peacefully days later, unrepentant, having outlived everyone who could prosecute him. Nash, arrested, asks Jonah only whether the town will hate him more than it loved him. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: hollow victory over a man already beyond judgment.

chapters.title: What the Town Decides
chapters.summary: Ashford convulses: resignations, a renamed civic center debate, families split. Some thank Jonah; more blame him. Okafor offers him a consultant's badge. He isn't ready to answer. POV: Jonah/town chorus. Emotional beat: the cost of truth counted publicly.

chapters.title: Reopening the Shop
chapters.summary: Jonah rebuilds the bookshop, shelving the recovered Marsh papers in a glass case labeled honestly: 'Ashford's Real History.' Cordelia visits, leaves without a word but donates anonymously to the restoration. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: quiet repair.

chapters.title: Felix and the Cipher
chapters.summary: Revealed: 'Felix' was the pen name Edmund Vane used for a single self-published novel, the very first edition that started everything—a confession disguised as fiction. Jonah reads it fully at last, closes the shop early, and walks the reservoir road as the sun sets, finally visible and unafraid. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: resolution—memory faced, identity chosen.
